ABSTRACT
The rapid proliferation of Internet of Things (IoT) devices has revolutionized wireless sensor networks (WSNs), enabling real-time
monitoring across various applications. However, this growth introduces critical security challenges, including data breaches, time
consumption, and memory overhead, which limit the efficiency and scalability of the existing encryption models. To address these
issues, this paper proposes a novel DNA-enclosed Fully Homomorphic Encryption (HD-FHE) scheme integrated with improved
elliptic curve cryptography (IECC). The proposed approach leverages dual-layer encryption by combining the strengths of deoxyri-
bonucleic acid (DNA) computing and homomorphic encryption to secure data processing without decryption. The IECC further
enhances key generation efficiency and reduces resource consumption. The experimental results demonstrate significant improve-
ments in encryption (1.675 ms for 3 KB) and decryption (1.582 ms for 3 KB) times, alongside high throughput (2.275 ms for 7 KB),
outperforming the existing models. These results highlight the robustness of the proposed method in minimizing vulnerabilities to
Chosen Plaintext Attack (CPA) and Chosen Ciphertext Attack (CCA) while ensuring scalability in dynamic IoT environments. This
work provides a significant contribution to IoT-based WSN security by achieving a balance between performance and protection,
paving the way for secure and efficient data transmission in next-generation networks.

Introduction
Cryptographic schemes are essential for securing communica-
tion in modern networks. Encryption techniques are utilized to
safeguard online activities such as browsing, emailing, setting up
virtual private networks (VPNs), and instant messaging, ensur-
ing the protection of telecommunications systems from various
threats [1]. In recent years, cryptography has proven to be a vital
tool for securing IoT devices, and it addresses challenges such
as scalability, computational demands, key management, and

light the need for more efficient cryptographic methods to meet

The integration of physical and digital systems in IoT environ-
ments transforms business operations, facilitating the rapid

critical applications [7]. However, as these IoT networks expand,
ensuring their security has become increasingly complex. Wire-

Cryptographic techniques, including encryption, authentication,
and key exchange mechanisms, become central in protecting data
integrity and maintaining secure communication across network
infrastructures [10–12]. Wireless sensor networks (WSNs) are
widely used in such applications due to their cost-effectiveness
and reliable management [13, 14]. However, combined encryp-
tion and compression watermarking raise concerns regarding
data security during transmission over IoT networks, highlight-
ing the need for stronger cryptographic designs [15]. The vast
amount of data collected by IoT devices and device-to-device
communication makes networks increasingly susceptible to
cyberattacks and also necessitates advanced cryptographic mea-
sures for detection and prevention [16]. As quantum computing
poses a potential risk to traditional cryptographic systems,
lattice-based cryptography has emerged as a promising solution
to maintain security in authentication and other cryptographic
processes [17]. Sometimes, machine learning and deep learning
models are also used to detect the possible attack that may occur
during the transaction [18].
Despite these advances, communication networks remain
vulnerable to data breaches and unauthorized access. This
underscores the continued importance of cryptographic solu-
tions in safeguarding privacy and preventing attacks [19, 20].
Achieving robust privacy protection and attack detection, par-
ticularly in domains involving data integrity and user privacy,
remains a complex challenge [21]. While wireless networks offer
significant advantages in terms of efficiency and scalability, they
also face heightened threats, especially in open networks such as
IoT, cloud computing, and big data environments [22, 23].
This paper proposes novel cryptographic approaches to enhance
the security and privacy of communication networks, partic-
ularly focusing on IoT and wireless networks. By addressing
current challenges in scalability, key management, and attack
detection, the work aims to improve the reliability of secure
communications in these environments.

Motivation and Problem Statement
When multiple network devices are connected, WSNs are crucial
to the real-time data collection process. In a WSN, the on-board
processor controls and monitors the local environment through
the use of sensor nodes. They communicate with the WSN
system’s central processing unit, the Base Station. To facilitate
data sharing, a WSN system’s base station is Internet-connected.
The data can be processed, analyzed, stored, and mined using
WSN. Therefore, WSN has a wide range of uses in the IoT for
monitoring and surveillance, including the detection of security
threats and environmental conditions (such as temperature,
humidity, air pressure, noise level, etc.) [24]. In addition, there
are a number of problems with WSN, such as inadequate energy
efficiency, poor network throughput performance, and node
failure, leading to complicated scalability when it comes to
large-scale deployment.
Consequently, the current approaches are susceptible to a range
of assaults, including eavesdropping, jamming, and spoofing.
The models encountered challenges, including a substantial
quantity of sensor nodes, in managing extensive data volumes.
Therefore, WSNs are frequently employed in contexts character-
ized by a high frequency of invasions from other wireless devices.
This can provide challenges in ensuring dependable communi-
cation among sensor nodes. Nevertheless, the current models
are susceptible to many security risks, including tampering and
denial of service attacks, which might potentially undermine the
confidentiality, integrity, and availability of data.
In order to overcome the security threats of the existing method-
ologies, the proposed work is intended to use secure encryption
schemes in which data is transmitted with low bandwidth and
high speed by implementing effective security measures. The
main contributions of the research paper are given as follows.
• To develop security and efficiency, an improved elliptic curve
cryptography (IECC) is modeled for public and private key
generation.
• To address challenges, such as time consumption, memory
overhead, and security issues, a hybrid DNA-enclosed Fully
Homomorphic Encryption (HD-FHE) approach is imple-
mented for data encryption.
• To ensure secure data processing, the HD-FHE method
combines DNA computing with homomorphic encryption,
which yields accurate decryption results.
Section 2 of the manuscript comprises the study of the existing
research, while Section 3 delves into the proposed methodology.
The outcomes and debates of the suggested models are shown
in Section 4, and the conclusion and future implications of the
suggested technique are covered in Section 5.

Related Works
A new Internet of Everything (IoE) big data security called
a DNA-based cryptographic scheme and access control model
(DNACDS) was discovered by Singh et al. [25] to counteract secu-
rity concerns. The data encryption step, in this case, was made up
of three parts: making the key, encrypting the data, and decrypt-
ing the data. Here, the permutation method underpinned both
the encryption and decryption stages, and the keys were not
sent via the communication channel, where the StSKAP protocol
served as the basis for key creation. While alternative DNA-based
security methods performed better in terms of encryption,
decryption, and data access times, the DNACDS model demon-
strated superior performance in these areas after the IoE frame-
work was put into place to provide secure cloud access.
Ghosh et al. [26] developed the Supervisory Control and Data
Acquisition (SCADA) model, which was a quantum-based
scheme with the entanglement of supersingular isogeny-based
cryptography. Hence, for communication, the secret key was

tion solution was introduced, and UML diagrams were used to
illustrate its features. By putting forth a new and secure dedu-

storage. This work provided effective and secure cloud storage

Cryptanalysis and Its Role in Encryption
Development
Cryptanalysis, the study of decoding encrypted information
without direct access to the decryption keys, plays a vital role in
evaluating the robustness of cryptographic schemes. Significant
advances in cryptanalysis research have identified vulnerabilities
in traditional encryption techniques and guided the development
of more secure models. Differential cryptanalysis method eval-
uates patterns in encryption to exploit weak keys. It is pivotal in
testing block ciphers, such as DES and AES. The linear cryptanal-
ysis technique identifies linear approximations in cipher struc-
ture and is commonly applied to symmetric encryption schemes.
Algebraic cryptanalysis exploits the algebraic structures partic-
ularly against public-key systems, such as RSA and lattice-based
approaches. Quantum cryptanalysis emerges with the advent of
quantum computing. It poses a threat to classical cryptographic
systems through algorithms like Shor’s, which can efficiently
factor

The novelty of the proposed method lies in its dual-layer encryp-
tion approach, which combines DNA encryption with fully
homomorphic encryption (FHE) to enable secure data processing
without decryption. This unique integration ensures robust pro-
tection against both classical and quantum cryptographic threats.
This capability lacks in the existing methods. Additionally, the
use of improved elliptic curve cryptography (IECC) for key gen-

IoT environments. By addressing challenges such as time con-
sumption, memory overhead, and vulnerability to CPA and CCA,
the proposed HD-FHE model achieves superior encryption and
decryption times while ensuring scalability and adaptability for
large-scale IoT deployments. These advancements distinguish
the proposed method from conventional models and offer a

Proposed Methodology
In order to make data transmission over the network faster and
more secure, this work suggests a novel approach that integrates
HD-FHE for encrypting and lowering the storage amount of data.
Data can be stored and transmitted using the contained DNA.
Due to the large number of unauthorized users and attackers on
the Internet, there are several security risks with IoT data. For
this reason, DNA cryptography is a state-of-the-art field for pro-
tecting sensitive information. When compared to conventional
encryption methods, homomorphic encryption offers superior
security. Similar to conventional encryption, homomorphic
encryption algorithms encrypt data using a public key. When
it comes to protecting networks, homomorphic cryptosystems
use more sophisticated mathematical techniques than standard
encryption. Further, for key generation, the IECC is utilized
for faster and smaller cryptographic keys. Then, the proposed
method HD-FHE combines DNA computing with homomorphic
encryption for accurate decryption results. Hence, the HD-FHE
enhances security, which helps to reduce the risk of data
breaches and protect sensitive data information from attack-
ers. Figure 1 displays the workflow diagram of the proposed
method.
Figure 1 illustrates the systematic workflow of the proposed
work. First, the data is encrypted with the generation of public
and private keys by using IECC for efficient cryptography. Sec-
ond, to enhance security-related issues, data encryption is done
by a hybridized model named HD-FHE for maintaining network
security. Then, the encrypted data can be processed by HD-FHE,
which helps in the production of decrypted results. Moreover, the
encrypted results are decrypted in order to yield secure outcomes.
Finally, the decrypted results show that the dual model is secure
for the transmission of data over computer networks.

Data Encryption
Data encryption is a way to keep secret information by encoding
it into ciphertext that can only be deciphered using a special key,
which is generated during encryption. Data encryption is the pro-
cess of transforming plaintext into ciphertext. The purpose of data
encryption is to safeguard sensitive information against unau-
thorized access. Cybersecurity architectures rely on encryption
as a first line of defense since it makes deciphering intercepted
data extremely challenging. Data encryption software, sometimes
called an encryption algorithm or cipher, is employed to create an
encryption scheme that might be cracked with substantial com-
putational resources.
3.2.1
|
Hybrid DNA-Enclosed Fully Homomorphic
Encryption
HD-FHE is an advanced encryption scheme that combines DNA
computing and Fully Homomorphic Encryption to enhance secu-
rity and efficiency in data processing. DNA computing uses par-
allelism with a high storage density of DNA molecules to per-
form complex computations, while FHE allows computations on
encrypted data without demanding decryption. By integrating
these technologies, HD-FHE ensures secure and efficient pro-
cessing of sensitive data. This enables an operation on encrypted
data to produce results that can be decrypted and also provides
robust security for various applications. Figure 2 shows how the
proposed approach’s structural design is implemented.

Results and Discussion
The results of the proposed method are compared with the other
existing models based on metrics like encryption time, decryption
time, throughput, CPA, and CCA. However, security measures
are used to protect data transmitted within WSNs. These results
validate the effectiveness of the proposed enhancements, high-
lighting their potential for deployment in numerous applications.
Training and testing use 80% and 20% of the produced datasets,
respectively.

Data Acquisition
The
dataset
used
for
evaluating
the
proposed
HD-FHE
model comprises encrypted data collected from a simulated
IoT-based wireless sensor network environment. The simu-
lation setup includes various IoT nodes, sensors, and base
stations to emulate real-world data transmission and encryption
scenarios.
The dataset characteristics are encrypted sensor readings and net-
work communication data. A total of 48,000 records are used
for analysis, encompassing various encryption levels and data
packet sizes. Key features include packet size, encryption type,
computational time, and throughput measures. Data is gen-
erated in a controlled IoT simulation environment using the
Python programming language. Preprocessing steps are applied
to ensure data quality and standardization. This includes nor-
malization of packet sizes and the removal of redundant or
corrupted entries. The dataset is divided into training (80%)
and testing (20%) subsets to validate the performance of the
proposed HD-FHE model. This dataset represents typical com-
munication and encryption patterns encountered in IoT-based
WSNs, ensuring the reliability and applicability of evaluation
results.

Performance Evaluation
Using a number of important measures, such as total execu-
tion time, CPU utilization, key generation time, encryption time,
and decryption time, the suggested HD-FHE is efficiently tested
and compared with current models. Both the encryption and
decryption timings are noticeably improved after the FHE is inte-
grated, since the time complexity is greatly reduced. Different
state of-the-art models are compared across the proposed model
to determine its efficiency.
4.2.1
|
Security Rate
In this study, the security rate refers to the effectiveness of the
encryption scheme in protecting IoT-based WSNs from potential
security threats such as unauthorized access, data tampering, and
eavesdropping. The security rate is quantified by the resistance
against cryptographic attacks, including brute force, side-channel
attacks, and man-in-the-middle attacks. Specifically, the security
rate is evaluated based on the computational complexity of the
encryption algorithm, with higher complexity corresponding to a
higher security rate. The security rate is evaluated by simulating
various cryptographic attacks using a network of 50 IoT nodes.
The security of the DNA-enclosed fully homomorphic encryp-
tion scheme is compared to traditional RSA and elliptic curve
encryption algorithms. The resistance to each attack is quantified
by measuring the number of cryptographic operations needed to
break the encryption. Additionally, entropy analysis is conducted
to assess the randomness of the ciphertext, providing a metric for
encryption strength.
4.2.2

Throughput
High throughput in the context of this study refers to the ability
of the IoT network to transmit data efficiently without causing
congestion or significant delays. Throughput is measured as the
data transfer rate, expressed in bits per second (bps). Through-
put is calculated by monitoring the rate at which encrypted data
is successfully transmitted over the sensor network while main-
taining a high level of security. A high throughput ensures that
data can be transferred quickly and securely, even as the number
of nodes in the network increases.
To assess high throughput, experiments are conducted in a sim-
ulated wireless sensor network with varying numbers of sensor
nodes and communication distances. The data transfer rate is
measured by transmitting encrypted sensor data across the net-
work and calculating the time required to successfully transfer a
fixed data packet between nodes. The throughput is then calcu-
lated as:
Throughput = Data transmitted∕Transmission time

Targeted Security Analysis
To assess the security of the proposed HD-FHE algorithm,
targeted analysis is conducted against common cryptanalytic
attacks:
1. Brute Force Attack: The use of Improved Elliptic Curve Cryp-
tography (IECC) ensures that the cryptographic keys have
sufficient complexity, mitigating brute force vulnerabilities.
Key size optimization in IECC reduces computational feasi-
bility for attackers.
2. Differential and Linear Cryptanalysis: The dual-layer struc-
ture of the HD-FHE model, integrating DNA encryption and
homomorphic encryption, introduces non-linear transfor-
mations and data permutation, making the model resistant
to differential and linear cryptanalytic approaches.
3. Quantum Resistance: The DNA-enclosed FHE integrates
advanced cryptographic techniques designed to counter
potential quantum cryptanalysis, such as Shor’s algorithm,
through increased randomness and structural complexity in
key generation.
4. Replay and Tampering Attacks: Integrity checks in the
encryption process safeguard against replay and tampering
attacks and ensure that the transmitted data remains unal-
tered.
This analysis confirms that the proposed HD-FHE algorithm
provides strong resistance to conventional and emerging crypt-
analytic techniques, reinforcing its applicability in securing
IoT-based WSNs.

Discussion
The paper introduces a hybrid encryption model called HD-FHE
combined with IECC for IoT-based WSNs, addressing critical
challenges such as security vulnerabilities, time consump-
tion, and memory overhead observed in existing models.
A key strength of the proposed approach is its dual-layer
encryption,
which
integrates
DNA
encryption
with
fully
homomorphic encryption, enabling secure data processing
without the need for decryption. This design ensures both high
security and efficiency, as demonstrated by its low encryption
and decryption times and improved throughput (1.646 ms for
3 KB, 2.101 ms for 5 KB, and 2.275 ms for 7 KB of data). These
improvements effectively tackle the high computational power
demands and low scalability noted in prior models, such as those
developed by Singh et al. [25], Ghosh et al. [26], and Khashan
et al. [27]. Additionally, the use of IECC for key generation
enhances the robustness of the security framework and makes it
highly suitable for IoT applications, which require reliable and
secure communication.
Assa-Agyei et al. [28] and Valluri et al. [29] addressed security
concerns in IoT networks that were resolved by the HD-FHE.
For instance, while scalability and efficiency are claimed as
strengths, a more detailed comparison of performance met-
rics, such as encryption time, memory usage, and resilience to
specific security threats like packet sniffing or replay attacks,
would better contextualize the improvements. Furthermore, a
critical analysis of the hybrid DNA-enclosed HD-FHE encryp-
tion addresses real-world IoT challenges, such as resource con-
straints and dynamic network conditions, which would rein-
force the claims of novelty and provide a clearer depiction of its
practical impact and significance. Table 4 shows the results of
a study that compares the performance of different models in

The proposed HD-FHE model is compared to many alternative
adaptive systems in this table. When compared to competing
models, the suggested one shows far better time efficiency. More-
over, the HD-FHE model is designed to address the privacy and
security challenges identified in the introduction. Specifically, it
tackles several critical issues within WSNs and IoT environments.
The encryption techniques employed in HD-FHE ensure that
data is transmitted in a secure manner, making it inaccessible to
unauthorized users. By utilizing strong cryptographic algorithms,
the model prevents eavesdropping on sensitive communications
and protects the confidentiality of the transmitted data. The inte-
gration of IECC in the HD-FHE model enhances node authen-
tication and secure key generation, thereby mitigating the risks
posed by Sybil and sinkhole attacks. The authentication process
ensures that only legitimate nodes can participate in the commu-
nication, thereby reducing the chances of these types of attacks.

Conclusion
This paper explores the potential of WSNs in Internet of Things
(IoT) systems, which are integral to enable efficient monitoring
and data collection across a wide range of applications. However,
WSNs are susceptible to numerous privacy and security chal-
lenges, such as eavesdropping, sinkhole attacks, Sybil attacks,
and clone attacks, which can compromise the integrity and confi-
dentiality of transmitted data. To address these concerns, a novel
hybrid model HD-FHE enhances data security through secure
encryption techniques. The integration of the IECC mechanism
further strengthens the model by generating secure keys and
applying advanced cryptographic techniques, thereby ensuring
robust protection against unauthorized access. The encrypted
data can subsequently be decrypted to retrieve the original infor-
mation without compromising security.
The evaluation of the proposed model demonstrates its effec-
tiveness, as it achieves high performance metrics, including
low encryption and decryption times, even as the size of the
data increases. Specifically, the model exhibits high throughput
(1.646 ms for 3 KB, 2.101 ms for 5 KB, and 2.275 ms for 7 KB),
fast encryption times (1.675 ms for 3 KB, 2.02 ms for 5 KB, and
0.66 ms for 7 KB), and efficient decryption times (1.582 ms for
3 KB, 1.823 ms for 5 KB, and 2.157 ms for 7 KB). Moreover, the
model effectively minimizes the Chosen Plaintext Attack (CPA)
and Chosen Ciphertext Attack (CCA) risks, ensuring secure com-
munication across diverse cryptographic schemes. This work
presents a significant contribution by enhancing the security of
sensitive data in WSNs while maintaining system efficiency and
dependability. However, there are still areas that require fur-
ther exploration. Future research can focus on optimizing the
proposed encryption techniques to further reduce resource con-
sumption, extend battery life, and enhance overall network effi-
ciency in WSNs. Additionally, incorporating adaptive security
measures and integrating real-time threat detection algorithms
can provide more dynamic responses to emerging threats in
IoT environments. These advancements would contribute to the
development of more resilient, secure, and intelligent IoT sys-
tems capable of supporting a broader range of applications.

Abstract: The rapid proliferation of Internet of Things (IoT) devices has revolutionized wireless sensor networks (WSNs), enabling real-time monitoring across various applications. However, this growth introduces critical security challenges, including data breaches, time consumption, and memory overhead, which limit the efficiency and scalability of the existing encryption models. To address these issues, this paper proposes a novel DNA-enclosed Fully Homomorphic Encryption (HD-FHE) scheme integrated with improved elliptic curve cryptography (IECC). The proposed approach leverages dual-layer encryption by combining the strengths of deoxyri- bonucleic acid (DNA) computing and homomorphic encryption to secure data processing without decryption. The IECC further enhances key generation efficiency and reduces resource consumption. The experimental results demonstrate significant improve- ments in encryption (1.675 ms for 3 KB) and decryption (1.582 ms for 3 KB) times, alongside high throughput (2.275 ms for 7 KB), outperforming the existing models. These results highlight the robustness of the proposed method in minimizing vulnerabilities to Chosen Plaintext Attack (CPA) and Chosen Ciphertext Attack (CCA) while ensuring scalability in dynamic IoT environments. This work provides a significant contribution to IoT-based WSN security by achieving a balance between performance and protection, paving the way for secure and efficient data transmission in next-generation networks.
